- Overestimate prices after recent spikes or bullish sentiment; model tends to overshoot in upward momentum phases.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is neutral or mildly bearish; model fails to adjust downward in low sentiment periods.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays downward revisions after negative sentiment spikes, especially in early days of a trend reversal.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp moves, leading to over-forecasted retracements in medium-term horizons.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly sensitive to recent sentiment swings, underperforming when sentiment is stable or slowly shifting.
- Avoid averaging sentiment across all days; weight recent sentiment more heavily for short-term correction.
- When sentiment drops below 0.3, reduce forecast slope; model tends to ignore bearish signals until they become entrenched.
- If sentiment is above 0.7 and price is rising, model often over-optimistic; cap forecast growth at 5–7% above recent peak unless sentiment confirms strong momentum.
